> **Community plugin v0.1.9** · Tag
>
> This release targets **DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2-rc.1** and add
s **individual member chat**: hover a Team in the composer, then select one member to run the Sessio
n as that member with its own role card, tools, Team Skills, and model route. It also moves member r
outing to `agent.model.select()` and per-step tool admission. Requires Agent Teams; keep 0.1.8 on ol
der hosts. Prebuilt artifacts are included.
### What's new in 0.1.9
- **Talk to one member directly.** The composer's Team picker now shows a member panel on hover. Sel
ecting a member injects its role card, tool policy, Team Skills, and model route into the current Se

ssion; selecting the captain keeps the Session model unchanged.
- **DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2-rc.1.** M
ember routes are recorded through `agent.model.select()` and tool admission is evaluated per step. T
he plugin refuses an unusable member route before applying anything instead of falling back to the c

aptain.
- **Custom tool policies are native-only.** On PTC presets the plugin preserves the deployme

nt's executor and explicitly refuses custom allow-lists; PTC still works with the all-tools mode.
-
**Built-in troubleshooting skill.** The global `agent-team-presets-troubleshooting` skill explains T
eam application, member creation, route evidence, Team Skill visibility, and install/upgrade failure
m application, member creation, route evidence, Team Skill visibility, and install/upgrade failures.
## Overview
**dsh-agent-team-presets** is a visual Team preset and private skill manager for DeepSeek Harness. C
onfigure a Team once, assign per-agent isolated skills, then select it from the conversation compose
r whenever you need it.
A Team contains a **captain** and any number of **member roles**:
- The captain uses the conversation's selected model, with its own role description, system prompt,

and tool policy.
- Each member can have an independent provider, model, reasoning effort, system pro

mpt, tool policy, and assigned Team Skills.
- The captain summons members through `spawn_team_member
`; native Agent Teams provides messaging, the shared task board, and runtime coordination.
This is a community plugin, not the Harness's bundled `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team-pres
ets` development package.
## Why this plugin?
DeepSeek Harness already ships Agent Teams with multi-agent collaboration. In the Harness versions t
his plugin supports, per-Team configuration, skill isolation, and reuse are still left to the user,
which is what this plugin addresses:
- **Teams are hard to reuse.** In those versions, native teams focus on runtime creation and collabo
ration, with no visual preset management; this plugin saves, duplicates, categorizes, and reuses nam

ed presets.
- **Role setup is repetitive.** Each role's name, description, system prompt, and tool p

olicies are configured once instead of re-described every time.
- **Splitting work across models is
awkward.** Every member picks its own model and reasoning effort, so one Team combines models by tas

k, while the captain keeps leading on the Session's model.
- **Tool permissions have no fine-grained
entry point.** In those versions the native tool surface offers no per-role allow-list; here the ca

ptain and each member carry their own, so roles differ in what they may use.
- **Skills lack per-age
nt scope isolation.** Shipped or user skills are typically registered globally, making all skills vi
sible to every agent; this plugin provides a private Team Skill library where skills are discovered

**only** by the specific Agent they are assigned to.
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements
- **DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.3.0`.** Verified against **`0.2.2-rc.1`**. Each member's route
is recorded through `agent.model.select()` for fresh, forked, and cold-resumed execution; the capta
in keeps the conversation's model selection. The plugin manager enforces `engines.dsh` from package.

json.
- **Custom tool allow-lists require a native Agent preset (standard or cordis).** This Host ca
nnot restore an inherited executor after a temporary override, so the plugin preserves the deploymen
t's executor and explicitly refuses custom policies on PTC. PTC remains available with the all-tools

mode. Select a native Agent preset before using custom policies.
- **Agent Teams enabled in the tar
get profile.** The standard integration is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team-profile`, which
supplies the Team service, tools, and Web roster. This plugin configures and manages Teams; it does

not replace that subsystem.
- **A Web or Desktop profile with Settings and the required client serv
ices.** Install into the profile you actually use, typically `web` for the Web GUI or `desktop` for

Desktop.
- **Durable storage and a continuable subagent backend for member execution.** Member creat
ion is refused if the storage domain or selected execution backend is unavailable. The default backe
nd names are `spawn` and `fork`.
The plugin version (`0.1.9`) and the Harness version (`0.2.2-rc.1`, for example) are separate versio
in version (`0.1.9`) and the Harness version (`0.2.2-rc.1`, for example) are separate version lines.
## Tool permissions and security
### Known limitation: Windows verification
The path-separator and executable-resolution fixes are exercised by unit tests that normalize separa
tors and by `ENOTDIR` cases, but no Windows machine was available here. Junction handling across vol
umes, `PATHEXT` resolution against a real `PATH`, and the full native build chain still need a Windo
ws run before the release is described as Windows-verified.
### Security boundaries
- The allow-list is **not a filesystem, process, or network sandbox**. Allowed tools (such as bash)

retain their native capabilities. Maintain appropriate Harness sandbox and approval policies.
- Cust
om policy mode disallows general-purpose `run_code` and ordinary `subagent` / `workflow` delegation

to preserve strict policy contracts. Use preset Team members for delegation.
- Managed members requi
re their durable configuration on resume. Missing or corrupted records are refused loud rather than
falling back to unrestricted defaults.
## Troubleshooting and limitations
